requirements.title: Establish and Maintain a Service Provider Management Policy
requirements.guidance: Govern the provider lifecycle consistently. Follow the approved provider policy.

operating_guidance.client_provider_split: Client defines policy and accepts contracts; providers supply security commitments.
operating_guidance.establish: Document inventory, classification, assessment, monitoring and decommissioning policy.
operating_guidance.operate: Follow the approved provider policy. The provider policy addresses classification, inventory, assessment, monitoring and decommissioning. This policy does not add the separate IG3 safeguards 15.5 through 15.7 to IG2.

requirements.official_text: Establish and maintain a service provider management policy. Ensure the policy addresses the classification, inventory, assessment, monitoring, and decommissioning of service providers. Review and update the policy annually, or when significant enterprise changes occur that could impact this Safeguard.

requirements.title: Classify Service Providers
requirements.guidance: Prioritize providers by relevant exposure. Classify providers and update changes.

operating_guidance.client_provider_split: Client defines policy and accepts contracts; providers supply security commitments.
operating_guidance.establish: Agree provider classification criteria.
operating_guidance.operate: Classify providers and update changes.

requirements.official_text: Classify service providers. Classification consideration may include one or more characteristics, such as data sensitivity, data volume, availability requirements, applicable regulations, inherent risk, and mitigated risk. Update and review classifications annually, or when significant enterprise changes occur that could impact this Safeguard.

requirements.title: Ensure Service Provider Contracts Include Security Requirements
requirements.guidance: Include security requirements in provider contracts consistent with the enterprise service provider management policy. Review contracts annually for missing requirements.

operating_guidance.client_provider_split: Client defines policy and accepts contracts; providers supply security commitments.
operating_guidance.establish: Identify required security terms and gaps.
operating_guidance.operate: Maintain contractual security commitments.

requirements.official_text: Ensure service provider contracts include security requirements. Example requirements may include minimum security program requirements, security incident and/or data breach notification and response, data encryption requirements, and data disposal commitments. These security requirements must be consistent with the enterprise’s service provider management policy. Review service provider contracts annually to ensure contracts are not missing security requirements.

requirements.title: Assess Service Providers
requirements.source_cadence: Source wording: annually, at a minimum, or with new and renewed contracts. Plan for annual coverage plus contract-triggered assessment; do not use contract renewal to excuse multi-year gaps.
requirements.guidance: Assess providers under the provider-management policy; reassess at least annually and address new or renewed contracts.

operating_guidance.accountable_role: Responsible client team or provider (client to identify)
operating_guidance.client_provider_split: Client approves scope and exceptions; the responsible client team or provider performs the activity and supplies relevant records.
operating_guidance.establish: Reconcile provider classifications to assessments, dates and contract events. Confirm the policy-defined depth is met and follow up missing, outdated or adverse results.
operating_guidance.operate: Assess providers under the provider-management policy; reassess at least annually and address new or renewed contracts. Source wording: annually, at a minimum, or with new and renewed contracts. Plan for annual coverage plus contract-triggered assessment; do not use contract renewal to excuse multi-year gaps.
operating_guidance.dependencies: Safeguard 15.1: Establish and Maintain an Inventory of Service Providers Safeguard 15.2: Establish and Maintain a Service Provider Management Policy

requirements.official_text: Assess service providers consistent with the enterprise’s service provider management policy. Assessment scope may vary based on classification(s), and may include review of standardized assessment reports, such as Service Organization Control 2 (SOC 2) and Payment Card Industry (PCI) Attestation of Compliance (AoC), customized questionnaires, or other appropriately rigorous processes. Reassess service providers annually, at a minimum, or with new and renewed contracts.

requirements.title: Monitor Service Providers
requirements.source_cadence: No fixed CIS interval. Follow the monitoring arrangements defined by the enterprise policy.
requirements.guidance: Monitor providers according to the enterprise provider-management policy.

operating_guidance.accountable_role: Responsible client team or provider (client to identify)
operating_guidance.client_provider_split: Client approves scope and exceptions; the responsible client team or provider performs the activity and supplies relevant records.
operating_guidance.establish: Identify the promised monitoring for each provider class and compare it with actual results and escalation. Review policy-defined timing without relabeling it as a CIS universal frequency.
operating_guidance.operate: Monitor providers according to the enterprise provider-management policy. No fixed CIS interval. Follow the monitoring arrangements defined by the enterprise policy.
operating_guidance.dependencies: Safeguard 15.1: Establish and Maintain an Inventory of Service Providers Safeguard 15.2: Establish and Maintain a Service Provider Management Policy

requirements.official_text: Monitor service providers consistent with the enterprise’s service provider management policy. Monitoring may include periodic reassessment of service provider compliance, monitoring service provider release notes, and dark web monitoring.

requirements.title: Securely Decommission Service Providers
requirements.source_cadence: Triggered by provider decommissioning. No recurring interval specified; the CAS twelve-month lookback is an assessment sample window.
requirements.guidance: End provider relationships securely.

operating_guidance.accountable_role: Responsible client team or provider (client to identify)
operating_guidance.client_provider_split: Client approves scope and exceptions; the responsible client team or provider performs the activity and supplies relevant records.
operating_guidance.establish: For a terminated provider, follow the relevant access, data-flow and data-disposition decisions through completion. If there were no terminations, examine readiness and record that operating evidence was unavailable.
operating_guidance.operate: End provider relationships securely. Triggered by provider decommissioning. No recurring interval specified; the CAS twelve-month lookback is an assessment sample window.
operating_guidance.dependencies: Safeguard 15.1: Establish and Maintain an Inventory of Service Providers Safeguard 15.2: Establish and Maintain a Service Provider Management Policy

requirements.official_text: Securely decommission service providers. Example considerations include user and service account deactivation, termination of data flows, and secure disposal of enterprise data within service provider systems.

requirements.title: Establish and Maintain a Secure Application Development Process
requirements.guidance: Make secure development repeatable. Follow secure lifecycle procedures.

operating_guidance.client_provider_split: Client owns delivery/security decisions; development team or contracted developer performs work.
operating_guidance.establish: Define development security process and responsibilities.
operating_guidance.operate: Follow secure lifecycle procedures. The development process addresses secure design, coding, developer training, vulnerability handling, third-party software security and application testing.

requirements.official_text: Establish and maintain a secure application development process. In the process, address such items as: secure application design standards, secure coding practices, developer training, vulnerability management, security of third-party code, and application security testing procedures. Review and update documentation annually, or when significant enterprise changes occur that could impact this Safeguard.

requirements.title: Establish and Maintain a Process to Accept and Address Software Vulnerabilities
requirements.source_cadence: Annual/change process review; intake when reports arrive.
requirements.guidance: Handle reported software weaknesses through resolution. Receive, assign, remediate and retest reports.

operating_guidance.client_provider_split: Client owns delivery/security decisions; development team or contracted developer performs work.
operating_guidance.establish: Establish external reporting path, triage, severity tracking and timing metrics.
operating_guidance.operate: Receive, assign, remediate and retest reports. Provide an external reporting channel and documented intake, ownership, remediation and retesting. Track severity and identification, analysis and remediation dates; review the handling process annually and after significant changes.

requirements.official_text:
Establish and maintain a process to accept and address reports of software vulnerabilities, including providing a means for external entities to report. The process is to include such items as: a vulnerability handling policy that identifies reporting process, responsible party for handling vulnerability reports, and a process for intake, assignment, remediation, and remediation testing. As part of the process, use a vulnerability tracking system that includes severity ratings, and metrics for measuring timing for identification, analysis, and remediation of vulnerabilities. Review and update documentation annually, or when significant enterprise changes occur that could impact this Safeguard.

Third-party application developers need to consider this an externally-facing policy that helps to set expectations for outside stakeholders.

requirements.title: Perform Root Cause Analysis on Security Vulnerabilities
requirements.source_cadence: When reviewing vulnerabilities; no numeric interval.
requirements.guidance: Address recurring causes of software vulnerabilities. Analyze causes and prevention actions.

operating_guidance.client_provider_split: Client owns delivery/security decisions; development team or contracted developer performs work.
operating_guidance.establish: Define root-cause responsibilities.
operating_guidance.operate: Analyze causes and prevention actions.

requirements.official_text: Perform root cause analysis on security vulnerabilities. When reviewing vulnerabilities, root cause analysis is the task of evaluating underlying issues that create vulnerabilities in code, and allows development teams to move beyond just fixing individual vulnerabilities as they arise.

requirements.title: Establish and Manage an Inventory of Third-Party Software Components
requirements.source_cadence: Evaluate component inventory at least monthly.
requirements.guidance: Know component dependencies and their risks. Check changes, updates and continued support.

operating_guidance.client_provider_split: Client owns delivery/security decisions; development team or contracted developer performs work.
operating_guidance.establish: Inventory current/planned third-party components and risks.
operating_guidance.operate: Check changes, updates and continued support. Track current and planned components, associated risks, updates and support status. Review component inventory at least monthly and identify unsupported components.

requirements.official_text: Establish and manage an updated inventory of third-party components used in development, often referred to as a “bill of materials,” as well as components slated for future use. This inventory is to include any risks that each third-party component could pose. Evaluate the list at least monthly to identify any changes or updates to these components, and validate that the component is still supported.

requirements.title: Use Up-to-Date and Trusted Third-Party Software Components
requirements.source_cadence: At component selection/use; no numeric interval.
requirements.guidance: Use trustworthy, maintained software dependencies. Obtain trusted, up-to-date components.

operating_guidance.client_provider_split: Client owns delivery/security decisions; development team or contracted developer performs work.
operating_guidance.establish: Define acquisition and vulnerability-evaluation practices.
operating_guidance.operate: Obtain trusted, up-to-date components. Use current trusted components and established frameworks or libraries where possible. Obtain components from trusted sources or evaluate vulnerabilities before use.

requirements.official_text: Use up-to-date and trusted third-party software components. When possible, choose established and proven frameworks and libraries that provide adequate security. Acquire these components from trusted sources or evaluate the software for vulnerabilities before use.

requirements.title: Establish and Maintain a Severity Rating System and Process for Application Vulnerabilities
requirements.source_cadence: Review severity system/process at least annually.
requirements.guidance: Prioritize application weaknesses and control releases. Triage vulnerabilities and apply release criteria.

operating_guidance.client_provider_split: Client owns delivery/security decisions; development team or contracted developer performs work.
operating_guidance.establish: Define severity model and minimum release acceptance.
operating_guidance.operate: Triage vulnerabilities and apply release criteria. Use a consistent vulnerability severity system with a minimum acceptance threshold for release; review the system annually.

requirements.official_text: Establish and maintain a severity rating system and process for application vulnerabilities that facilitates prioritizing the order in which discovered vulnerabilities are fixed. This process includes setting a minimum level of security acceptability for releasing code or applications. Severity ratings bring a systematic way of triaging vulnerabilities that improves risk management and helps ensure the most severe bugs are fixed first. Review and update the system and process annually.

requirements.title: Use Standard Hardening Configuration Templates for Application Infrastructure
requirements.guidance: Use industry-recommended hardening templates for application infrastructure: underlying servers, databases, web servers, cloud containers, Platform as a Service (PaaS) and Software as a Service (SaaS) components. In-house developed software must not weaken configuration hardening.

operating_guidance.client_provider_split: Client owns delivery/security decisions; development team or contracted developer performs work.
operating_guidance.establish: Adopt industry-recommended hardening templates for underlying servers, databases, web servers, cloud containers, PaaS and SaaS application components.
operating_guidance.operate: Maintain application infrastructure hardening across the covered components. Do not allow in-house developed software to weaken configuration hardening.

requirements.official_text: Use standard, industry-recommended hardening configuration templates for application infrastructure components. This includes underlying servers, databases, and web servers, and applies to cloud containers, Platform as a Service (PaaS) components, and SaaS components. Do not allow in-house developed software to weaken configuration hardening.

requirements.title: Separate Production and Non-Production Systems
requirements.guidance: Separate live and non-live application environments. Maintain environment separation.

operating_guidance.client_provider_split: Client owns delivery/security decisions; development team or contracted developer performs work.
operating_guidance.establish: Define production/non-production boundaries.
operating_guidance.operate: Maintain environment separation.

requirements.official_text: Maintain separate environments for production and non-production systems.

requirements.title: Train Developers in Application Security Concepts and Secure Coding
requirements.guidance: Equip developers to write secure code. Deliver environment-specific developer training.

operating_guidance.client_provider_split: Client owns delivery/security decisions; development team or contracted developer performs work.
operating_guidance.establish: Identify development roles and relevant training.
operating_guidance.operate: Deliver environment-specific developer training.

requirements.official_text: Ensure that all software development personnel receive training in writing secure code for their specific development environment and responsibilities. Training can include general security principles and application security standard practices. Conduct training at least annually and design in a way to promote security within the development team, and build a culture of security among the developers.

requirements.title: Apply Secure Design Principles in Application Architectures
requirements.source_cadence: During design; no numeric interval specified.
requirements.guidance: Build security into application architecture. Apply principles through design and change.

operating_guidance.client_provider_split: Client owns delivery/security decisions; development team or contracted developer performs work.
operating_guidance.establish: Define secure design principles and review responsibility.
operating_guidance.operate: Apply principles through design and change. Apply least privilege, check access at each operation, validate untrusted input type, size, range and format, and minimize exposed functionality.

requirements.official_text: Apply secure design principles in application architectures. Secure design principles include the concept of least privilege and enforcing mediation to validate every operation that the user makes, promoting the concept of "never trust user input." Examples include ensuring that explicit error checking is performed and documented for all input, including for size, data type, and acceptable ranges or formats. Secure design also means minimizing the application infrastructure attack surface, such as turning off unprotected ports and services, removing unnecessary programs and files, and renaming or removing default accounts.

requirements.title: Leverage Vetted Modules or Services for Application Security Components
requirements.source_cadence: At selection/use; no numeric interval specified.
requirements.guidance: Use established security building blocks. Maintain use of proven identity, crypto and audit capabilities.

operating_guidance.client_provider_split: Client owns delivery/security decisions; development team or contracted developer performs work.
operating_guidance.establish: Identify vetted security modules/services.
operating_guidance.operate: Maintain use of proven identity, crypto and audit capabilities. Use vetted identity, cryptographic, audit and logging modules with accepted reviewed algorithms; avoid custom security implementations.

requirements.official_text: Leverage vetted modules or services for application security components, such as identity management, encryption, and auditing and logging. Using platform features in critical security functions will reduce developers’ workload and minimize the likelihood of design or implementation errors. Modern operating systems provide effective mechanisms for identification, authentication, and authorization and make those mechanisms available to applications. Use only standardized, currently accepted, and extensively reviewed encryption algorithms. Operating systems also provide mechanisms to create and maintain secure audit logs.

requirements.title: Implement Code-Level Security Checks
requirements.source_cadence: Within the application lifecycle; no fixed calendar frequency or universal every-commit rule specified.
requirements.guidance: Use both static and dynamic code-analysis tools during the application lifecycle to check secure coding.

operating_guidance.accountable_role: Responsible client team or provider (client to identify)
operating_guidance.client_provider_split: Client approves scope and exceptions; the responsible client team or provider performs the activity and supplies relevant records.
operating_guidance.establish: Review the application/release population and where each analysis type operates. Trace representative results to triage and relevant remediation, without requiring a new Omnisciente integration.
operating_guidance.operate: Use both static and dynamic code-analysis tools during the application lifecycle to check secure coding. Within the application lifecycle; no fixed calendar frequency or universal every-commit rule specified.
operating_guidance.dependencies: Safeguard 2.1: Establish and Maintain a Software Inventory

requirements.official_text: Apply static and dynamic analysis tools within the application life cycle to verify that secure coding practices are being followed.

requirements.title: Conduct Application Penetration Testing
requirements.source_cadence: No fixed frequency specified in 16.13. Use application/program requirements; do not import the annual infrastructure-test interval as this safeguard's wording.
requirements.guidance: Perform application penetration testing, considering authenticated testing for critical applications and manual tester analysis.

operating_guidance.accountable_role: Responsible client team or provider (client to identify)
operating_guidance.client_provider_split: Client approves scope and exceptions; the responsible client team or provider performs the activity and supplies relevant records.
operating_guidance.establish: Identify tested applications, criticality, authentication coverage and manual business-logic exploration. Review test scope, findings and follow-up; distinguish scanning from penetration testing.
operating_guidance.operate: Perform application penetration testing, considering authenticated testing for critical applications and manual tester analysis. No fixed frequency specified in 16.13. Use application/program requirements; do not import the annual infrastructure-test interval as this safeguard's wording.
operating_guidance.dependencies: Safeguard 2.1: Establish and Maintain a Software Inventory

requirements.official_text: Conduct application penetration testing. For critical applications, authenticated penetration testing is better suited to finding business logic vulnerabilities than code scanning and automated security testing. Penetration testing relies on the skill of the tester to manually manipulate an application as an authenticated and unauthenticated user.

requirements.title: Conduct Threat Modeling
requirements.source_cadence: During design, before coding. No fixed calendar interval specified.
requirements.guidance: Have specially trained people model application threats and address design flaws before code is created.

operating_guidance.accountable_role: Responsible client team or provider (client to identify)
operating_guidance.client_provider_split: Client approves scope and exceptions; the responsible client team or provider performs the activity and supplies relevant records.
operating_guidance.establish: Inspect a design-stage model, participants' relevant training, entry points and access levels. Trace identified design risks to decisions before implementation.
operating_guidance.operate: Have specially trained people model application threats and address design flaws before code is created. During design, before coding. No fixed calendar interval specified.
operating_guidance.dependencies: Safeguard 2.1: Establish and Maintain a Software Inventory

requirements.official_text: Conduct threat modeling. Threat modeling is the process of identifying and addressing application security design flaws within a design, before code is created. It is conducted through specially trained individuals who evaluate the application design and gauge security risks for each entry point and access level. The goal is to map out the application, architecture, and infrastructure in a structured way to understand its weaknesses.

requirements.title: Designate Personnel to Manage Incident Handling
requirements.guidance: Identify incident leadership, backup coverage and internal oversight.
requirements.official_text: Designate one key person, and at least one backup, who will manage the enterprise’s incident handling process. Management personnel are responsible for the coordination and documentation of incident response and recovery efforts and can consist of employees internal to the enterprise, service providers, or a hybrid approach. If using a service provider, designate at least one person internal to the enterprise to oversee any third-party work. Review annually, or when significant enterprise changes occur that could impact this Safeguard.

requirements.title: Establish and Maintain Contact Information for Reporting Security Incidents
requirements.guidance: Verify incident notification contacts.
requirements.official_text: Establish and maintain contact information for parties that need to be informed of security incidents. Contacts may include internal staff, service vendors, law enforcement, cyber insurance providers, relevant government agencies, Information Sharing and Analysis Center (ISAC) partners, or other stakeholders. Verify contacts annually to ensure that information is up-to-date.

requirements.title: Establish and Maintain an Enterprise Process for Reporting Incidents
requirements.guidance: Document and communicate the workforce incident-reporting process.
requirements.official_text: Establish and maintain an documented enterprise process for the workforce to report security incidents. The process includes reporting timeframe, personnel to report to, mechanism for reporting, and the minimum information to be reported. Ensure the process is publicly available to all of the workforce. Review annually, or when significant enterprise changes occur that could impact this Safeguard.

requirements.title: Establish and Maintain an Incident Response Process
requirements.guidance: Coordinate complete incident response. Execute response process during incidents.

operating_guidance.client_provider_split: Client retains oversight; internal responders/provider coordinate assigned response duties.
operating_guidance.establish: Document response roles, obligations and communications.
operating_guidance.operate: Execute response process during incidents. Document response roles, compliance obligations and communications, and review the response process annually and after significant changes.

requirements.official_text: Establish and maintain a documented incident response process that addresses roles and responsibilities, compliance requirements, and a communication plan. Review annually, or when significant enterprise changes occur that could impact this Safeguard.

requirements.title: Assign Key Roles and Responsibilities
requirements.guidance: Make incident roles and handoffs explicit. Activate assigned roles during incidents.

operating_guidance.client_provider_split: Client retains oversight; internal responders/provider coordinate assigned response duties.
operating_guidance.establish: Agree cross-functional and provider responsibilities.
operating_guidance.operate: Activate assigned roles during incidents. Include relevant legal, IT, security, facilities, public relations, HR, responders, analysts and third-party responsibilities.

requirements.official_text: Assign key roles and responsibilities for incident response, including staff from legal, IT, information security, facilities, public relations, human resources, incident responders, and analysts. Review annually, or when significant enterprise changes occur that could impact this Safeguard.

requirements.title: Define Mechanisms for Communicating During Incident Response
requirements.guidance: Keep incident communications usable during disruption. Use available incident communication channels.

operating_guidance.client_provider_split: Client retains oversight; internal responders/provider coordinate assigned response duties.
operating_guidance.establish: Define primary and fallback communication methods.
operating_guidance.operate: Use available incident communication channels. Define primary and alternate incident communication channels, accounting for unavailable or compromised email.

requirements.official_text: Determine which primary and secondary mechanisms will be used to communicate and report during a security incident. Mechanisms can include phone calls, emails, secure chat, or notification letters. Keep in mind that certain mechanisms, such as emails, can be affected during a security incident. Review annually, or when significant enterprise changes occur that could impact this Safeguard.

requirements.title: Conduct Routine Incident Response Exercises
requirements.guidance: Exercise incident decisions and coordination. Run exercises covering channels, decisions and workflows.

operating_guidance.client_provider_split: Client retains oversight; internal responders/provider coordinate assigned response duties.
operating_guidance.establish: Plan realistic scenarios, participants and objectives.
operating_guidance.operate: Run exercises covering channels, decisions and workflows. Conduct actual exercises at least annually that test communications, decisions and response workflows; track resulting improvements.

requirements.official_text: Plan and conduct routine incident response exercises and scenarios for key personnel involved in the incident response process to prepare for responding to real-world incidents. Exercises need to test communication channels, decision making, and workflows. Conduct testing on an annual basis, at a minimum.

requirements.title: Conduct Post-Incident Reviews
requirements.source_cadence: After incidents; no fixed calendar interval.
requirements.guidance: Learn from actual incidents. Capture lessons and assign improvements.

operating_guidance.client_provider_split: Client retains oversight; internal responders/provider coordinate assigned response duties.
operating_guidance.establish: Define post-incident review responsibility.
operating_guidance.operate: Capture lessons and assign improvements. After incidents, capture lessons and follow up improvements. The safeguard does not prescribe a separate fixed numeric review interval.

requirements.official_text: Conduct post-incident reviews. Post-incident reviews help prevent incident recurrence through identifying lessons learned and follow-up action.

requirements.title: Establish and Maintain Security Incident Thresholds
requirements.source_cadence: Annually, or when significant enterprise changes could affect the safeguard. Preserve both planned review and change-triggered review.
requirements.guidance: Define and maintain incident thresholds distinguishing incidents from events; review annually and after relevant significant changes.

operating_guidance.accountable_role: Responsible client team or provider (client to identify)
operating_guidance.client_provider_split: Client approves scope and exceptions; the responsible client team or provider performs the activity and supplies relevant records.
operating_guidance.establish: Confirm the event/incident distinction is usable by responders and linked to the response process. Check the last review and relevant changes; keep CAS prioritization/escalation prompts separate from the safeguard minimum.
operating_guidance.operate: Define and maintain incident thresholds distinguishing incidents from events; review annually and after relevant significant changes. Annually, or when significant enterprise changes could affect the safeguard. Preserve both planned review and change-triggered review.
operating_guidance.dependencies: Safeguard 17.4: Establish and Maintain an Incident Response Process

requirements.official_text: Establish and maintain security incident thresholds, including, at a minimum, differentiating between an incident and an event. Examples can include: abnormal activity, security vulnerability, security weakness, data breach, privacy incident, etc. Review annually, or when significant enterprise changes occur that could impact this Safeguard.

requirements.title: Establish and Maintain a Penetration Testing Program
requirements.source_cadence: Program-defined frequency; no separate numeric minimum in 18.1.
requirements.guidance: Make penetration testing purposeful and controlled. Maintain the testing program.

operating_guidance.client_provider_split: Client authorizes tests and priorities; qualified tester executes; owners remediate.
operating_guidance.establish: Agree scope, frequency, limits, contacts, remediation and retrospectives.
operating_guidance.operate: Maintain the testing program. Scale testing to organizational size, complexity, industry and maturity. Define network, application, API, hosted and physical scope where relevant, frequency, testing limits and hours, excluded attacks, contacts, remediation routing and retrospective review.

requirements.official_text: Establish and maintain a penetration testing program appropriate to the size, complexity, industry, and maturity of the enterprise. Penetration testing program characteristics include scope, such as network, web application, Application Programming Interface (API), hosted services, and physical premise controls; frequency; limitations, such as acceptable hours, and excluded attack types; point of contact information; remediation, such as how findings will be routed internally; and retrospective requirements.

requirements.title: Perform Periodic External Penetration Tests
requirements.guidance: Have qualified testers probe external exposure. Execute external penetration tests.

operating_guidance.client_provider_split: Client authorizes tests and priorities; qualified tester executes; owners remediate.
operating_guidance.establish: Select qualified party and authorize scope/limits.
operating_guidance.operate: Execute external penetration tests. At least annually, use qualified external testers and include reconnaissance of the enterprise and its environment.

requirements.official_text: Perform periodic external penetration tests based on program requirements, no less than annually. External penetration testing must include enterprise and environmental reconnaissance to detect exploitable information. Penetration testing requires specialized skills and experience and must be conducted through a qualified party. The testing may be clear box or opaque box.

requirements.title: Remediate Penetration Test Findings
requirements.source_cadence: After findings, on risk-prioritized remediation timelines.
requirements.guidance: Resolve penetration-test weaknesses by risk. Remediate penetration-test findings.

operating_guidance.client_provider_split: Client authorizes tests and priorities; qualified tester executes; owners remediate.
operating_guidance.establish: Define finding ownership and routing.
operating_guidance.operate: Remediate penetration-test findings. Prioritize test findings by risk and apply documented vulnerability remediation timelines and effort according to impact and priority.

requirements.official_text: Remediate penetration test findings based on the enterprise’s documented vulnerability remediation process. This should include determining a timeline and level of effort based on the impact and prioritization of each identified finding.

requirements.title: Validate Security Measures
requirements.source_cadence: After each penetration test. No fixed number of days for follow-up specified.
requirements.guidance: Validate defenses after every penetration test; adjust detection rules or capabilities when needed.

operating_guidance.accountable_role: Responsible client team or provider (client to identify)
operating_guidance.client_provider_split: Client approves scope and exceptions; the responsible client team or provider performs the activity and supplies relevant records.
operating_guidance.establish: Match each completed test to a defense-validation result. Check whether techniques used were detected and whether necessary changes were made; include application tests where relevant.
operating_guidance.operate: Validate defenses after every penetration test; adjust detection rules or capabilities when needed. After each penetration test. No fixed number of days for follow-up specified.
operating_guidance.dependencies: Safeguard 18.1: Establish and Maintain a Penetration Testing Program

requirements.official_text: Validate security measures after each penetration test. If deemed necessary, modify rulesets and capabilities to detect the techniques used during testing.

requirements.title: Perform Periodic Internal Penetration Tests
requirements.source_cadence: No less than annually; more frequent testing follows the program where specified.
requirements.guidance: Perform internal penetration tests under the program at least annually.

operating_guidance.accountable_role: Responsible client team or provider (client to identify)
operating_guidance.client_provider_split: Client approves scope and exceptions; the responsible client team or provider performs the activity and supplies relevant records.
operating_guidance.establish: Verify internal scope, test completion date and alignment with the program; inspect findings and their follow-up. Keep external and internal test coverage separately visible.
operating_guidance.operate: Perform internal penetration tests under the program at least annually. No less than annually; more frequent testing follows the program where specified.
operating_guidance.dependencies: Safeguard 18.1: Establish and Maintain a Penetration Testing Program

requirements.official_text: Perform periodic internal penetration tests based on program requirements, no less than annually. The testing may be clear box or opaque box.
